problem:
Let 
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}].$ 
Which of the following statements are true?

- $det(A)=0$
- $A$ is invertible
- $Ax=b$ has exactly one solution for any $2\times 1$ column vector $b$
worked_solution:
Recall that given $A=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{11} & {a}_{12} \\ {a}_{21} & {a}_{22}\end{aligned}]$, then according to the invertible matrix theorem the following statements are equivalent:    

- $A$ is invertible.

- The system $Ax=b$ has exactly one solution for any $2\times 1$ column vector $b.$

- The system $Ax=0$ has the unique zero solution.

- The lines ${a}_{11}x+{a}_{12}y={b}_{1}$ and ${a}_{21}x+{a}_{22}y={b}_{2}$ intersect at exactly one point.

- $det(A)\ne 0.$

With that in mind, let's now check our statements.

- Statement I is false. We have 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =det[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =2\cdot 3-(-3)\cdot 2 \\  & =12\ne 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the fifth part of the invertible matrix theorem is true, all the other parts of the theorem are true too. Therefore, according to the theorem:

- Statement II is true by the first part of the invertible matrix theorem.

- Statement III is true by the second part of the invertible matrix theorem.

Finally, only statements II and III are true.
